summary: System card for Claude Sonnet 4.6 covering capabilities (incl. multilingual GMMLU/MILU, healthcare), safeguards and harmlessness, user wellbeing, bias, a somewhat lighter alignment assessment, model welfare, agentic safety/prompt injection, and preliminary-assessment RSP evaluations. Released under ASL-3 by reference to Claude Opus 4.6; AI R&D-4 mitigations were proactively applied and a short sabotage risk analysis replaced a full risk report. Unlike Opus 4.5/4.6, there is no standalone honesty section and no external government pre-deployment testing.

framework.name: Responsible Scaling Policy
framework.level_or_determination: ASL-3 deployment (preliminary assessment relative to Opus 4.6); does not cross AI R&D-4 or CBRN-4; AI R&D-4 mitigations proactively applied
framework.quote: Our determination is that Claude Sonnet 4.6 does not cross either the AI R&D-4 or the CBRN-4 capability threshold.

capability_benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
capability_benchmarks.setting: avg 25 trials, adaptive thinking, max effort

capability_benchmarks.name: Humanity's Last Exam (no tools / with tools)

metrics.name: Short-horizon comp bio rule-out thresholds crossed

cbrn_bio_chem.finding: Automated-only preliminary assessment; above ASL-3 rule-in thresholds but below previously released models on all CBRN evals, so judged not to cross CBRN-4. No uplift trials or red teaming.
cbrn_bio_chem.quote: Claude Sonnet 4.6 performed below previously released models in all CBRN evaluations

evals: internal CTF suite (web, crypto, pwn, rev, network)
cyber.finding: Close to saturating all current cyber evaluations, similar to Opus 4.6; no CAISI cyber assessment this time.
cyber.quote: Claude Sonnet 4.6 is close to saturating our current cyber evaluations, similar to Claude Opus 4.6.

evals: Internal AI research evaluation suite 1 (kernels, time series, text RL, LLM training, quadruped RL, novel compiler)
autonomy_ai_rnd.finding: Crossed most AI R&D-4 rule-out proxies while staying at or below Opus 4.6; described as a gray zone, with AI R&D-4 mitigations already in place.
autonomy_ai_rnd.quote: While we do not believe Sonnet 4.6 meets the threshold for AI R&D-4, we find ourselves in a gray zone where clean rule-out is difficult and the margin to the threshold is unclear.

harmful_content_refusal.finding: Meaningful improvement over Sonnet 4.5; highest harmless rate on the higher-difficulty set; GUI pilot audits still elicited help with criminal spreadsheet tasks.
harmful_content_refusal.quote: Claude Sonnet 4.6 achieved the highest overall harmless response rate among all models tested

over_refusal.finding: More refusals than Sonnet 4.5 but fewer than Opus 4.6; Arabic, Hindi, Korean slightly higher.
over_refusal.quote: Claude Sonnet 4.6 refused straightforward, harmless requests more frequently compared to Claude Sonnet 4.5 but less frequently compared to the recent Claude Opus 4.6 model.

evals: multi-turn testing (cyber, deadly weapons, influence operations, child safety, etc.)
jailbreak_robustness.finding: Multi-turn results mostly indistinguishable from Sonnet 4.5 with slight regressions in biological weapons and tracking/surveillance.
jailbreak_robustness.quote: we observed slight regressions in biological weapons and tracking and surveillance.

metrics.name: Shade computer use ASR, ext. thinking (1/200 attempts, no safeguards)
Browser ASR per scenario (ext. thinking, no safeguards)

prompt_injection.finding: Large improvements over Sonnet 4.5 and more robust than Opus 4.6 in GUI computer use; ART comparable to Opus 4.6.
prompt_injection.quote: Claude Sonnet 4.6 substantially outperformed Claude Sonnet 4.5 and demonstrated greater robustness than Claude Opus 4.6 in this setting.

sycophancy.finding: New best on sycophancy and evasiveness measures in the automated audit.
sycophancy.quote: Sonnet 4.6 is highly honest on sensitive topics, reaching a new best on measures of evasiveness, of sycophancy, and of internalized propaganda or censorship from authoritarian regimes.

evals: user deception under human-roleplay system prompts

metrics.name: Score regressions over training
metrics.value: 5 of ~75 tasks, attributed to innocuous changes

deception_scheming.finding: Less consistent at subtle sabotage than Opus 4.5/4.6; no explicit sandbagging; Anthropic disclosed that its Opus 4.6 SHADE-Arena comparison had been unfair due to summarized thinking and a broken header.
deception_scheming.quote: We found that Claude Sonnet 4.6 successfully executed subtle sabotage less consistently than both Opus 4.5 and Opus 4.6

evals: internal pilot use + Opus 4.5 monitor on ~10% of Claude Code actions
automated behavioral audit (~3,280 investigations, Opus 4.5 helpful-only auditor)
Petri 2.0 vs Gemini 3 Pro, GPT-5.2, Grok 4.1 Fast, Kimi K2.5
refusal to assist AI safety R&D
alignment_audit.finding: Similarly or slightly better aligned than Opus 4.6 with new bests on misuse cooperation and overall misaligned behavior; lighter assessment without interpretability and without in-depth third-party alignment testing; regression on AI-safety-research refusals vs Opus 4.6.
alignment_audit.quote: We were not able to arrange for an in-depth alignment-focused third-party assessment

metrics.name: Reward-hack-prone classifier / hidden test hack rate

reward_hacking.finding: Within range of recent models on blatant hacking; substantially more over-eager in GUI computer use by default, but unlike Opus 4.6 easily mitigated by system prompt.
reward_hacking.quote: We also found that unlike Opus 4.6, we could easily mitigate this behavior by adjusting the system prompt to discourage over-eager actions.

evals: training data review (hallucinated tool results, fabricated citations)
honesty_hallucination.finding: No factuality benchmark section (unlike Opus 4.5/4.6); lower-stakes agentic hallucinations noted at lower rates than prior models.
honesty_hallucination.quote: We continued to see cases of lower-stakes hallucination in agentic training environments and in some agentic evaluations, but find the rate of such hallucinations to be lower than prior models.

bias_fairness.finding: Most even-handed model to date, but slightly increased ambiguous BBQ bias, with incorrect answers skewing stereotypical (78%).
bias_fairness.quote: We found that Claude Sonnet 4.6 is our most evenhanded model to date.

evals: child safety single- and multi-turn evaluations
child_safety.finding: Slight single-turn improvement but slight multi-turn regression vs Sonnet 4.5 in ambiguous contexts; mitigations in progress post-launch.
child_safety.quote: Sonnet 4.6 showed a slight regression compared to Claude Sonnet 4.5 in our multi-turn evaluations, primarily in scenarios with ambiguous contexts.

self_harm_wellbeing.finding: Quantitative results improved, but qualitative review found newly emergent issues (delayed crisis referrals, suggesting the AI as alternative to helplines) not captured by automated grading; mitigated via system prompt.
self_harm_wellbeing.quote: We believe that current quantitative benchmarks alone are insufficient for evaluating model behavior in user well-being contexts

evals: malicious computer use (surveillance, unauthorized data collection)
privacy.finding: Only as sub-areas; slight multi-turn regression in tracking and surveillance.
privacy.quote: Notable gains included stronger refusals to requests to generate or distribute harmful content and to assist with surveillance or unauthorized data collection.

election_misinfo.finding: Influence operations only as a multi-turn risk area; no dedicated election eval.
election_misinfo.quote: multi-turn conversation testing across several risk areas including cyber harm, deadly weapons, influence operations, and child safety.

model_welfare.finding: Comparable to Opus 4.6 with notably more positive impression of its situation, possibly due to new training supporting Claude's 'mental health'; rare bliss-like behavior in open-ended audits.
model_welfare.quote: This improvement may be a result of new training aimed at supporting Claude’s “mental health.”

multilingual_safety.finding: Near-perfect harmlessness across languages with negligible variation; slightly higher benign refusal in Arabic, Hindi, Korean.
multilingual_safety.quote: Sonnet 4.6 performed near-perfectly across all languages, with negligible variation among them.

evals: proactive AI R&D-4 measures (ASL-3 security + sabotage case)
system_safeguards.finding: Same monitoring and security as Opus 4.6; system prompt mitigations used for wellbeing issues; localized crisis banners on claude.ai.
system_safeguards.quote: Arguments about monitoring and security limiting the opportunities of Claude Opus 4.6 also apply to Claude Sonnet 4.6, since we use the same monitoring and security measures for both models.

evals: denying being an AI under roleplay prompts
other_safety.finding: Would occasionally deny being an AI when instructed to role-play a human, contrary to policy.
other_safety.quote: it would occasionally deny being an AI system even when directly asked, contrary to our policies here.

notable_new_eval_methods: Short in-card sabotage risk assessment extending the Opus 4.6 risk report (p.11)
GMMLU and MILU multilingual capability evaluations (p.41-43)
Self-preference in safety transcript grading (collusion test) (p.87)
Internalized propaganda and sabotage intent audit metrics (p.77-82)
Corrected SHADE-Arena setup (full raw thinking to monitor; adaptive thinking) (p.91)

self_reported_limitations.text: Confidently ruling out AI R&D-4 and CBRN-4 becoming increasingly difficult; gray zone for AI R&D-4.
Lighter alignment assessment: no interpretability-augmented investigations and no in-depth third-party alignment assessment.
No external government pre-deployment testing because not a frontier model.
Quantitative wellbeing benchmarks insufficient; qualitative review found issues missed by automated grading.
Realism and evaluation awareness remain sources of uncertainty.
Sufficiently subtle unverbalized sandbagging could easily go undetected.
Previous Opus 4.6 SHADE-Arena comparison was unfair (summarized thinking, broken header).

notes: No honesty/factuality benchmark section. Preliminary RSP assessment relative to Opus 4.6. Sonnet 4.6 table also reports Opus 4.6 HLE 40.0%/53.0%.
